The main takeaway from our work is that
the linkless embedding conjecture is equivalent to the following statement: A graph admits a panelled embedding if and only of it contains no minor from a certain list of seven graphs.

the linkless embedding problem is a natural and useful way to study the topology of graphs embedded in 3-dimensional space, and that the linkless and panelled embedding properties are topological invariants in the sense that they can be detected from the fundamental group.

the linkless embedding conjecture is a special case of the more general panelled embedding conjecture, which is in turn a special case of a conjecture of Scharlem ann and Thompson on the fundamental group of the complement of a graph in 3-space.
